newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwaitis like strike on Iraq, want Saddam out.
newsitem.headline: Kuwaitis like strike on Iraq, want Saddam out.

text.p: Kuwaitis were happy with Tuesday's U.S. missile attack on Iraq and said they want to see President Saddam Hussein toppled instead of hearing about one-off strikes against their former occupier.
"Stalling does not pay. I wish there were many more (strikes) to remove Saddam once and for all," Mariam al-Wagayan, a Kuwaiti civil servant, said.
"It is not enough to say he (Saddam) deserves that."
Her remarks echoed the thoughts of many Kuwaitis whose memories of Iraq's 1990-91 occupation remain vivid.
"I support the strike 100 percent. I only wish that Saddam is toppled. He is the big head," said Mohammad Subhi who works for Kuwait's municipality.
"He is sitting there torturing people. Is that a right thing to do?"
The Kuwaiti government said it "fully understood" the U.S. attack.
"Kuwait reaffirms the necessity of Iraq's full compliance with all international resolutions to ensure peace and stability in the region," a cabinet statement said.
Few Kuwaitis shared the view of other governments in the Arab world that denounced the attack.
"Saddam should be hit personally. The Iraqi people have no link (to Iraqi policies). As an Arab I am in solidarity with the Iraqi people," said Mohammad Ali, a National Bank of Kuwait employee.
"Saddam is in his hiding. Who received the strike? It is the Iraqi people...What is happening has no justice in it."
There were no signs of panic in Kuwait. However, businessmen expressed some concern about the impact on business.
"I hope this doesn't spread. We need stability in this region," said businessman Waleed al-Huwail.
